crossroad-escapables.name: Crossroad Escapables
crossroad-escapables.heroSubtitle: Real-time multiplier curves, fast round resolution, and OpenRNG-backed fairness for crash-style gameplay.

steps.title: Create a Crash Round
steps.description: From your backend, call POST /v1/engines/crossroad-escapables/rounds with the playerId, currency, and wager. Store the returned roundId in your own database.

steps.title: Subscribe to Round Updates
steps.description: Use webhooks or polling on GET /v1/engines/crossroad-escapables/rounds/{roundId} to track round state and crashPoint. Your frontend uses this to animate the curve.

steps.title: Handle Cashouts
steps.description: When a player presses “Cash Out”, send POST /v1/engines/crossroad-escapables/rounds/{roundId}/cashout from your backend. If successful, credit the payout to the player ledger.

steps.title: Settle & Reconcile
steps.description: Listen for round.completed webhooks to confirm final results. Use these events as a source of truth for accounting and dispute resolution.

web2.title: Web2: Custodial Casino / Aggregator
web2.subtitle: Best for traditional platforms that already manage accounts, KYC, and balances.
bullets: Players sign in using your existing account system; you own KYC and AML.
Your frontend renders the crash UI and talks only to your backend (never directly to MonkGames).
Your backend calls MonkGames crash APIs server-to-server, using your API keys and internal playerId references.
All money lives in your cashier or wallet system; MonkGames never holds funds — we only compute outcomes.
You listen to round.* webhooks and update your own ledger for wagers, wins, and refunds.
Use this model if you operate fiat, off-chain tokens, or any fully custodial environment.

web3.title: Web3: Wallet-Based or Hybrid
web3.subtitle: Best for dapps and operators where the player’s wallet is the source of truth.
bullets: Players connect a web3 wallet (e.g. MetaMask, WalletConnect). You map walletAddress → internal playerId in your backend.
Your smart contract or backend escrows the wager (on-chain or in a custodial balance) before calling MonkGames.
Your backend still calls MonkGames APIs server-to-server, but attaches metadata like walletAddress and txHash for traceability.
On round completion, you verify the result and then trigger on-chain settlement via your own contract logic.
You can optionally publish MonkGames RNG proofs or round hashes on-chain for verifiable transparency.
Use this model if you want crash gameplay that feels web3-native but keeps heavy math and regulation in your backend.

items.description: Initialises a new crash round for a specific player and wager.
Attempts to cash the player out before the crash point is reached.
Fetches the current or final state of a crash round.

items.description: Your internal identifier for the player account.

items.name: currency
items.description: ISO code or token symbol used for wagers (e.g. USD, EUR, USDT).

items.name: wager
items.description: Amount to stake on the round in the smallest unit of the selected currency.

items.name: roundId
items.description: Identifier of the crash round returned from the create call.

webhooks.title: Crash Engine Webhooks
webhooks.subtitle: Use these events to update balances and analytics in real time.

events.description: Emitted when a crash round is created and scheduled.
Fires when the multiplier reaches the crash point.
Contains final settlement information including payout multipliers and results.

notes.title: Implementation Notes & Best Practices
bullets: Only your backend should call the crash engine APIs; never expose API keys to the client.
Use idempotency keys on create-round requests to protect against retries and double wagers.
Treat webhooks as the source of truth for accounting, with periodic reconciliation against your own ledger.
You can run multiple market-specific themes on top of the same crash engine configuration.

drawballz-rushmore.name: Drawballz | Rushmore Classics
drawballz-rushmore.heroSubtitle: Instant and scheduled draw formats with OpenRNG-powered outcomes and themeable tickets, rooms, and mascots.

steps.title: Create a Ticket
steps.description: From your backend, call POST /v1/engines/drawballz-rushmore/tickets with playerId, currency, wager, and poolId. The response includes ticketId and optionally an inline result for instant games.

steps.title: Track Draw Status
steps.description: For scheduled draws, poll GET /v1/engines/drawballz-rushmore/draws/{drawId} or subscribe to draw.completed webhooks.

steps.title: Fetch Ticket Results
steps.description: Use GET /v1/engines/drawballz-rushmore/tickets/{ticketId} to retrieve matched balls, prize tier, and payout information for your player.

steps.title: Credit Winnings
steps.description: When a ticket is marked as settled, credit winnings to the player balance in your cashier or wallet systems and log the result for audits.

web2.title: Web2: Hosted Casino / Lottery Operator
web2.subtitle: Best for operators that already run centralized lottery or instant-win games.
bullets: Players log in using your existing account; you maintain player profiles, limits, and KYC.
Your lobby or game page calls your backend to buy tickets; the backend calls MonkGames ticket APIs with your playerId.
You keep all money in your own balance system; MonkGames only provides outcomes and prize tiers.
You can map MonkGames poolId and tier to your own product catalog and bonus / loyalty systems.
Webhooks such as draw.completed and ticket.settled drive balance updates and notification emails or SMS.
Use this model if you are replacing or upgrading existing instant-lotto or keno-style content.

web3.title: Web3: On-Chain Pools & Tickets
web3.subtitle: Best for dapps that want transparent, ritual-style draws powered by player wallets.
bullets: Players join pools using a wallet, sending funds into your draw smart contract or a custodial pool.
Your backend or an off-chain service calls MonkGames APIs with a playerId that is mapped to walletAddress on your side.
When draws complete, you receive draw.completed and ticket.settled webhooks and update on-chain state via contract calls.
You can publish round hashes and winning numbers on-chain to keep a verifiable public record.
Advanced setups can let players verify that their ticket commitment was included in the pool before the draw.
Use this model if you want festival-style, community draws that feel native to on-chain ecosystems.

webhooks.title: Draw Engine Webhooks
webhooks.subtitle: Receive updates when draws close and tickets resolve.

notes.title: Implementation Notes & Best Practices
bullets: For scheduled draws, use webhooks as the primary signal and the draw status endpoint as a backup.
Map prize tiers into your own accounting system rather than relying solely on raw payouts.
Pools and draw schedules can be configured per market; speak with MonkGames if you need custom calendars.
Tickets, rooms, and mascot themes can be swapped without changing underlying pool math or compliance settings.
